status: DRAFT — UNSIGNED (automated execution; human review and signature outstanding)

body.anaDetail: No AI provider is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or AI_BEDROCK_ENABLED / AI_VERTEX_ENABLED) — without one, every AnA turn returns 503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE. OPENAI_API_KEY or KIMI_API_KEY alone answer chat but not regulatory drafting, which only an approvedForHighRisk model may serve.

steps.title: Anonymous access refused
steps.action: GET /api/cmc/drug-substances without Authorization
steps.observed: HTTP 401

steps.title: The programme and its reference records
steps.action: POST /api/c2c/projects, then the drug substance, product, method, specification, batch and stability under it
steps.expected: created; every row carries the programme
steps.observed: programme 78731580-7719-4562-985d-a412edebff5a with 6 reference records

steps.title: A read-only session reads every register and writes none
steps.action: as the viewer (OQ_VIEWER): GET each register's list for the programme, then POST a drug substance under it; as the run identity, list the drug substances
steps.expected: each read 200; the write 403 and no row written
steps.observed: drug-substances 200; drug-products 200; analytical-methods 200; specifications 200; batch-records 200; stability-studies 200; the viewer's write 403 , no row
steps.note: v0.11: the reads and the write are the viewer's (until v0.10 the step read with the run session and never wrote). The specification and batch-record lists are /:projectId routes, not ?projectId= (server/api/cmc/specificationRoutes.ts, batchRecordRoutes.ts): v0.1 read GET /api/cmc/specifications, which is no route, and was answered 404.

steps.title: A programme of another organisation is not found
steps.action: GET and POST a register under a programme id this organisation does not hold
steps.expected: the read names no record of that programme (404/403, or 200 with nothing); the write is refused and no row is written
steps.observed: read 200; write 409

steps.title: Each register write reaches Module 3 as a canonical source only
steps.action: GET /api/cmc/module3-os/source-evidence/:programme and the sections, before any compile
steps.expected: one canonical source per recorded row; no section record yet
steps.observed: 0 sections before compile; source-evidence 200

steps.title: One deterministic compile from the programme’s own records
steps.action: POST /api/cmc/module3-os/compile/:programme, then read the sections
steps.expected: the core §3.2.S / §3.2.P / 3.1 / 3.3 sections, the emittable 3.2.A appendices and US 3.2.R; each completeness is the compiler’s

steps.title: A compile with nothing recorded is refused and says what to record
steps.action: create a second IND programme with no CMC records and compile it
steps.expected: 409 naming the registers to record first; nothing written
steps.observed: 409: No canonical source objects for this project — nothing to compile. Record the project's CMC data in the registers (substance, product, methods, specifications, batches, stability);

steps.title: A biologic programme composes nothing
steps.action: create a programme with productType biologic, record a mAb, compile
steps.expected: 409 CMC_PRODUCT_CLASS_OUT_OF_SCOPE; nothing composed; the refusal names ICH Q6B and the authoring path
steps.observed: 409 CMC_PRODUCT_CLASS_OUT_OF_SCOPE; 0 sections; This project records its product as a biologic, and Module 3 is composed here only for a drug (a small-molecule medicinal product). A biologic's quality require

steps.title: A marketing application, and a substance whose modality is not established
steps.action: compile an NDA programme; then a drug programme whose substance records no route
steps.expected: 409 CMC_APPLICATION_OUT_OF_SCOPE, then 409 CMC_MODALITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED; nothing composed
steps.observed: NDA CMC_APPLICATION_OUT_OF_SCOPE; no route recorded CMC_MODALITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED

steps.title: A request body cannot supply a section’s record or its completeness
steps.action: refresh a section with a body claiming completeness 100 and missingInputs []
steps.expected: the stored record is the composer’s; the body’s claim is not written
steps.observed: §3.2.S.1 refresh 200; stored completeness 100 unchanged

steps.title: An approval states its own reason
steps.action: approve a section with no reason, then with a 7-character reason
steps.expected: 400 REASON_REQUIRED naming the field; both refused with nothing written
steps.observed: no reason 400 REASON_REQUIRED (field reason); a 7-character reason 400 REASON_REQUIRED

steps.title: Identity is not authority
steps.action: as a member without signing authority: approve a section
steps.expected: 403 ESIGNATURE_NO_AUTHORITY; no signature row
steps.observed: the member's approval 403 ESIGNATURE_NO_AUTHORITY; signature rows 0 → 0
steps.note: v0.11: the approval is the member's (OQ_MEMBER). Until v0.10 it was sent with the run session, an organisation admin, which holds signing authority.

steps.title: A section approval is an electronic signature
steps.action: as the signer: approve with a wrong password, then with the password and a fresh authenticator code
steps.expected: 401 then 200; the section approved; one electronic_signatures row with the signer, the meaning and the bound digest; a chained audit row; a version snapshot
steps.observed: wrong password 401; signed 200; version 8742e751-3bb6-4345-9815-1028d0772d33; 1 signature row(s)

steps.title: The bound digest is a digest of the stored section version
steps.action: as the runtime role (DATABASE_URL_RUNTIME, the organisation set as the server sets it): read the signature row's bound digest and the approved version's stored snapshot; recompute the §11.70 digest
steps.expected: the signature row carries a sha256 bound digest, basis cmc-module3-section-version-sha256, equal to sha256 of the canonical JSON of {organizationId, projectId, sectionKey, versionNumber, approvedVersionId, snapshot}
steps.observed: signature 50: stored 01bec5cd54f72b0b… = recomputed over version 8742e751-3bb6-4345-9815-1028d0772d33 (v1)
steps.note: v0.11: no product read serves the bound digest (GET /api/part11/signatures/by-target does not return bound_payload_digest) or the stored snapshot (there is no versions route), so the step reads both as the runtime role, under row-level security, and recomputes the digest with the product's recipe (server/api/cmc/module3OperatingSystemRoutes.ts, the section approval; canonicalJson from tests/validation/lib/qms-digest.mjs). Until v0.10 it read the digest from the by-target read and a versions route, neither of which serves it.

steps.title: What the signer read is what is signed
steps.action: as the signer: approve a section sending the content hash read before a recompile
steps.expected: 409 SECTION_CHANGED; nothing signed
steps.observed: 409 SECTION_CHANGED; §3.2.A.1 still draft

steps.title: The sweep reports what it examined and keeps a recorded resolution
steps.action: sweep; re-sweep; compare what each reports
steps.expected: the sweep reports what it examined; a recorded resolution survives the re-run
steps.observed: the sweep reports {"specifications":1,"methods":1,"stability":1,"batches":1,"comparability":0}; re-sweep 200

steps.title: Resolving a critical finding needs signing authority and a reason
steps.action: resolve a critical finding as a member, then as the signer
steps.expected: 403 ESIGNATURE_NO_AUTHORITY with the row still open and no audit row; then resolved with a reason and a chained row

observed.details: 1 analytical method(s) lack validated status: RP-HPLC Assay. Specifications reference these methods.

steps.deviationReason: not executed — the reference records raise no critical contradiction, so the credentialed resolve has nothing to act on.

steps.title: The final-export gate names every blocker
steps.action: the gate with one section approved and the rest not
steps.expected: 409 naming the blocker; 200 only when every blocker is clear
steps.observed: 409: 20 of 21 sections unapproved, 3 without source lineage; sentence: 3 section(s) have no recorded source lineage, so the audit trail required for export is incomplete

steps.title: Placement writes the approved sections into the programme’s own sequence
steps.action: place the approved Module 3 into the programme’s IND sequence; then retry with the same key
steps.expected: 200 with one leaf per placed section; the retry idempotent

observed.error: 3 section(s) have no recorded source lineage, so the audit trail required for export is incomplete

steps.deviationReason: not executed — the placement was refused 409 by the final-export gate (1 of 21 sections approved, 3 without source lineage) and wrote no leaf, which is the designed answer. The reference records do not compose a Module 3 whose every section can be approved, so the positive placement and its idempotent retry were not observed. A fixture for it is owed.

steps.title: Placement requires the regulatory-author role
steps.action: as the viewer, who holds no regulatory-author role: place
steps.expected: 403; no leaf written
steps.observed: 403 ; leaves 0 → 0
steps.note: v0.11: the placement is the member's (OQ_MEMBER). Until v0.10 it was sent with the run session. v0.12: the placement is the viewer's (OQ_VIEWER). An organisation member holds the regulatory-author role (ORG_ROLE_FUNCTIONAL_GRANTS, server/middleware/auth.ts), so OQ_MEMBER passed the role and was answered by the export gate (409); the viewer is the identity without it. The step depends on the approval (OQ-CMC-13), not on a completed placement: the role is refused before the target is read, and the step needs only the sequence OQ-CMC-19 creates.

steps.title: The version history and the provenance events are append-only in the database
steps.action: as the runtime role: UPDATE and DELETE on cmc_module3_section_versions and cmc_provenance_events
steps.expected: each refused by the database
steps.observed: cmc_module3_section_versions.UPDATE refused: 42501; cmc_module3_section_versions.DELETE refused: 42501; cmc_provenance_events.UPDATE refused: 42501; cmc_provenance_events.DELETE refused: 42501

steps.title: A batch release rests on recorded, reviewed QC results and happens once
steps.action: release over results that are not recorded; then create a batch already released
steps.expected: 409 each time; nothing released
steps.observed: release with no QC result 409; create already released 409

steps.title: Editing an approved specification withdraws the approval, with the reason recorded
steps.action: as the signer, validate the specification's analytical method on its register; approve the specification; then widen its limits without a reason, then with one
steps.expected: the method validated 200; the approval 200; 422 without a reason; with one, the edit lands and the approval is withdrawn
steps.observed: method validated 200; approved 200; edit with no reason 422; with a reason 200 and the approval withdrawn (undefined)
steps.note: v0.11: since d9060a85e2 (2026-11-08, F1) and P-110 item 1 (2026-11-09) a specification is approved only when the method it names is in the project's register and validated, or shown suitable, under signature; the step validates OQ-CMC-03's method through the register's signed Validate act first. Until v0.10 the approval was the first act.

steps.title: The deterministic engines cite what they judged and refuse a foreign programme
steps.action: the ICH compliance check for the programme, then for a programme of another organisation
steps.expected: it cites the guideline revision and the records it judged; 403/404 for the foreign programme
steps.observed: compliance 200 citing guidelines; a nonexistent programme 404 with no records; a foreign programme 404

steps.title: The Overview and Module 3 build screens tell the truth about their own state
steps.action: load the CMC screens for the programme, and for a programme with nothing recorded
steps.expected: the approvals, portfolio, build state and the gate’s own readiness verdict are shown; an uncomputed figure says so; a never-swept programme is not reported as swept and clear
steps.observed: screens captured for the recorded and the empty programme; the reviewer reads the screenshots

steps.title: Only the interview that commits is offered
steps.action: read the deployment posture, then start the CMC interview and an interview of a kind that reaches no record
steps.expected: the CMC interview starts; the other interview is refused LAUNCH_SCOPE, naming where its answers would have gone
steps.deviationReason: not executed — the interview and its refusal are both reachable only through an AnA turn, and no AI provider is configured (/readyz reports ana down), so every AnA turn answers 503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE and no interview starts. Observe this under the W3 posture with a provider configured.

steps.title: A release signature covers the manifest that would be transmitted
steps.action: sign the sequence’s release, then read the dispatch gate
steps.expected: the signature is bound to this sequence’s leaf manifest; a manifest that differs reads as no release signature for the sequence
steps.observed: prerequisite step OQ-CMC-19 did not pass

steps.title: An original IND carrying no 3.2.S and no 3.2.P is not dispatch-ready
steps.action: read the dispatch readiness of the original IND sequence
steps.expected: the verdict speaks to the Module 3 requirement, citing 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) and (b) and naming both remedies
steps.observed: prerequisite step OQ-CMC-19 did not pass

steps.title: The surface claims only the paths its screens call
steps.action: with launch scope enforced: a path the CMC screens call, and a path under /api/cmc that no screen claims
steps.expected: the called path served; the unclaimed path 403 LAUNCH_SCOPE
steps.observed: claimed 200; unclaimed 403 LAUNCH_SCOPE

steps.title: A submission package carries Module 3 only when the gate is open
steps.action: an orchestrator run carrying inline CMC data, then a run over the programme
steps.expected: inline data 400 INLINE_CMC_SOURCES_REFUSED; the run composes no Module 3 and says the gate refused it
steps.deviationReason: not executed — this is a development server (its CSP is report-only), which allows inline cmcSources (it answered 400 invalid_request), the documented development behaviour. The refusal is a production control; observe it on a production build.

steps.title: Every register create names the person who recorded it
steps.action: read the chained audit ledger after the prerequisite’s writes
steps.expected: one row per recorded row, naming the operator and the record; none anonymous; the chain verifies
steps.observed: 6/6 records named by a register-create row; 151 rows, none anonymous; chain ok over 1078 row(s) of audit_logs

steps.title: The approver is not one of the people who entered the records
steps.action: as the author who recorded the registers: approve a section; then with the meaning authorship
steps.expected: 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES naming why; then 400 APPROVAL_IS_NOT_AUTHORSHIP; nothing signed either time
steps.observed: self-approval 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES; authorship meaning 400 APPROVAL_IS_NOT_AUTHORSHIP; §3.2.S.1 still draft

steps.title: Anything the tester observed that no step above covers
steps.action: the tester records it here
steps.expected: reviewer judgment
steps.observed: the run’s own identifiers are attached for the reviewer; the runner records no further observation

steps.title: A register record cannot be born, or edited, into its signed state
steps.action: on each of analytical methods, process validation and comparability: create with the register’s signed word (and its signer and date) in the body, then edit an ordinary record into it; then create a QC result already carrying reviewedBy
steps.expected: each refused 409 naming the governed path that does record it; nothing written, and no signer or date set
steps.observed: 4 registers refuse the signed state on create; 3 refuse it on an edit; each names its own governed path

steps.title: The signature the refusal names records the signer, and closes the record
steps.action: sign each of the three through the path its refusal named: with no reason, with a reason but no re-authentication, with both but without the thing the signature accepts, then with everything; then edit the signed record
steps.expected: the signature records the status, the signer and the date, writes one electronic_signatures row bound to the chained audit row, and the edit after it is refused
steps.observed: 3 registers signed through the path their refusal named; each records the signer and refuses the edit after

steps.title: A shelf-life claim is judged against the data the studies cover
steps.action: record four programmes: a shelf-life claim within the long-term coverage, one beyond it, one beyond it with no accelerated study, and one whose claim is free text that states no period; read the ICH compliance verdict for each
steps.expected: Q1E pass, then a finding naming the months claimed and the months covered, then a second finding that Q1E admits extrapolation only on accelerated data, then not_evaluated quoting the text it could not read — never a pass
steps.observed: 4 stability programmes judged: within=pass, beyond=warning, noaccel=warning, unreadable=not_evaluated, planned=warning
steps.note: v0.11: each programme records its small-molecule drug substance before its studies. Since ef71545c8e (2026-10-22) the composition boundary holds at every CMC entry point, the ICH compliance check included: a project that records no drug substance is answered 409 CMC_MODALITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED, because whether its Module 3 is composable here is not established.

steps.title: An ordinary register edit records who changed it, and what moved
steps.action: edit one record in each of three registers — a serial one, a uuid one, and one moved by two fields at once — then send the same body again; then edit a record that does not exist; read each record’s chained history back
steps.expected: one act per edit that moved something, each naming the actor, the fields that moved and both values; the repeat body adds no act; the unknown record is a 404 that adds none; every act is sealed into the tenant chain
steps.observed: 3 registers record an edit with both values; a repeat body records none; chain ok over 1117 row(s)

steps.title: A record’s change history is readable against the record it is about
steps.action: read the change history through the product’s own route for each edited record, then ask it for a record that does not exist and for a register that keeps no history; read the specifications register’s own history route
steps.expected: the create and each edit in order with the person, the fields and both values; 404 for the unknown record; 404 naming the registers that do keep one — never an empty history; the specifications route still answers 200
steps.observed: 3 record histories read in order; an unserved register names the served ones; specifications 200

steps.title: No verdict and no filing for a programme the organisation does not hold
steps.action: ask for an ICH compliance verdict, a QbD derivation and a control strategy, and file a container closure, a comparability assessment and a material specification, under programme ids the organisation does not hold; then the same six under the run’s own programme; and one create with no programme at all
steps.expected: each read 404 stating nothing was assessed and each create 409 naming the programme as not this organisation’s, with nothing written; the same six succeed under the run’s own programme; the create with no programme is accepted as an organisation-wide record
steps.observed: 3 unheld programme(s) × 6 paths refused; the same 6 serve this run's own programme; an org-wide record is accepted

steps.title: A stability study’s shelf life is recorded under a signature
steps.action: create a study already COMPLETED with a shelf life, then close an ordinary study out by PUT; then sign the close-out with no reason, with a reason but no re-authentication, with both but no shelf life recorded, with a shelf life but no results pulled, and with everything; then edit the closed-out study and close it out again
steps.expected: the create and the PUT are each refused 409 naming POST /api/cmc/stability-studies/:id/close-out and nothing is stored; then 400, then 401, then 409 naming the missing shelf life, then 409 naming the absent results, then 200 with COMPLETED, the signer and the date set and one electronic_signatures row; the edit after is 409 SIGNED_RECORD and a second close-out is 409 already COMPLETED
steps.observed: the close-out is a signature: refused on the create, on the edit, with no reason, with no re-authentication, over no claim and over no data; once signed, closed and unrepeatable

steps.title: The composed section says whether its shelf-life claim was signed for
steps.action: record the same shelf-life claim, the same three pull-point results and the same condition on two programmes, close one out under a signature, and compose §3.2.P.8 for each
steps.expected: both sections state the period and the data it is subject to review of; the signed one reads "accepted on a signed study close-out" and the running one "recorded on a study that has not been closed out under signature" — the only difference between the two sections
steps.observed: two programmes identical but for the signature compose two different §3.2.P.8 provenance statements

steps.title: Agency questions on Module 3 are the letter's record; the earlier CMC file is read-only
steps.action: POST and PATCH /api/cmc/agency-questions; as the runtime role, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on reg_questions (each rolled back); log a response-required letter on the programme and record a question on it at §3.2.P.7; set its owner to a member of the organisation with a reason; read the programme's Module 3 questions
steps.expected: 410 CMC_QUESTION_FILE_READ_ONLY twice with the earlier file unchanged; the runtime role refused by the database; 201 for the question; 200 for the owner; the Module 3 read lists it at §3.2.P.7 from the question, unanswered, not overdue, with that owner
steps.observed: legacy POST 410, PATCH 410; reg_questions.INSERT refused: 42501; reg_questions.UPDATE refused: 42501; reg_questions.DELETE refused: 42501; reg_questions.TRUNCATE refused: 42501; question 5 listed at §3.2.P.7, unanswered
